string.equality.ref: JavaScript strings are values: two equal strings are never different references.
boxing.equality: Values are not boxed in JavaScript: two boxed equal numbers compare equal by reference too.
float.precision: `float` is a JavaScript number, so it keeps double precision instead of rounding to single.
array.outofrange: Array accesses are not bounds-checked: reading past the end gives undefined instead of throwing IndexOutOfRangeException.
exception.null.deref: Dereferencing null throws a JavaScript TypeError, not a NullReferenceException.
dict.insertion.order: After a Remove, .NET reuses the freed slot for the next Add; that order is unspecified in .NET, and JavaScript keeps insertion order.
generic.default: Generics are erased: default(T) inside generic code is null for value types too.
enum.getvalues: Enums are erased to numbers: a boxed or generic enum value formats as its number.
list.capacity.tostring: No runtime type names: Object.ToString on a type that does not override it does not give the .NET type name.
object.tostring.default: No runtime type names: Object.ToString on a type that does not override it does not give the .NET type name.
gettype.name: No reflection: GetType() is not available in JavaScript.
span.sum: Span<T> and stackalloc are not supported.
